title: Task context for task-oriented experience extraction
description: Describes the downstream task an experience library is being built for. Deliberately bench-independent: no field names a dataset, metric implementation, or harness. Switching benchmarks means writing a different instance of this file, never editing extraction code. Passing no context at all restores bench-blind extraction.

task.description: What the downstream agent must produce, in task terms rather than dataset terms.

objective.description: The quantity the attempt is judged on.

direction.description: Which way is better on `objective`. Requires `objective`.

data_characteristics.description: Properties of the input that bear on method choice: scale, length, dimensionality, noise, available history. Used to decide applicability boundaries.

reference_points.description: Known values on the objective, as label -> value. Read by the extractor as a ceiling check: if a family of simple methods already reaches some value well short of the target, experience about tuning that family further is low value.

bottlenecks.description: What currently limits performance, stated as an obstacle rather than a fix -- the same pre-solution wording the record schema's `trigger_context` uses.

extraction_focus.description: What this pass should bias toward. Separate from `bottlenecks` because a bottleneck is an observation while this is an instruction.
